chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isa from Zur'ah from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who freed one-third of her servant upon death. Is it upon her family to manumit her (kitabah)? He said: 'That is not for her, but she is entitled to one-third of her value, so let her serve according to the calculation of what was freed from her.'

key_terms.يُكَاتِبُوهَا: To enter into a contract of manumission (kitabah) with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave woman who is partially freed in her owner's will upon death?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between partial manumission via will (*wasiyya*) and the contractual manumission (*kitabah*) initiated by the slave. He establishes that the heirs are not obligated to enter a *kitabah* contract for the freed third; instead, the slave retains a proportional ownership stake in her own value, necessitating continued service to the heirs commensurate with the portion that remains enslaved. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that partial freedom creates a co-ownership structure rather than an automatic transition to full liberty or a mandatory redemption contract.
